cells.tense: The ledger is open on the table and the pen is in your hand.
cells.ask: Keep one measure you already hold to — the one most yours — and hold it on purpose for a week, out loud where it costs you something small.
cells.core:
On an ordinary day you notice a small unfairness and correct it with one move — a word to the right person, a line redrawn — and then you keep walking. The compass is working and the direction holds steady. What it hands you next is the harvest: what you've been quietly keeping fair can now be gathered and used, not just maintained.

The work is to keep one measure on purpose, in the open, where it can be seen and answered. Holding a thing fair is one thing; saying that you're the one holding it is another, and the second is what a balance like this one can feed next.
cells.sheetLine: Your sense of what's fair is working, and it's yours to keep.
cells.verb: Weighing what's fair in the private ledger and letting it point the way
cells.place: In the pull toward what you actually want, the light you steer by

cells.tense: You're already at the hearing that hasn't started, bracing for a verdict you can't write in.
cells.ask: Before you decide what's owed in one situation you've been weighing, ask someone who was there what they saw — and let their account stand without correcting it.
cells.core:
When the compass runs fast, you've already run the whole ledger in your head — what they gave, what you owe, what it means about you — before anyone has said a word. You replay the uneven trade and add it to a column that keeps growing. The fairness you're chasing is starting to cost you the people you're measuring.

Fairness here doesn't need a verdict before the facts are in. What calms this is support from outside your own figuring: one account that isn't yours, allowed to stand. Ask, and let it land as information rather than as another item to weigh — the point is to be in the exchange, not to win it.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping score on a game that hasn't been played yet.
cells.verb: Weighing what's fair in the private ledger and letting it point the way

cells.tense: You're still at a door that closed behind you, watching for it to reopen.
cells.ask: Name one exchange you've been treating as already settled — the one you've quietly crossed off — and say one plain sentence of what you'd actually want from it, out loud, even if only you hear it.
cells.core:
In the balance, you name what's fair as it happens and let it move through you. Trades stay in motion, and the light stays where you can see it. Lately the compass has gone quiet: the weighing stopped, and whatever needed evening out got stepped around instead.

Backing the sense of fairness into the light doesn't mean charging it up by force. It means a small discipline outside the silence — one clear statement of what's fair, said in your own words, with a beginning and an end. Whatever wish for things to come even is still in you; speaking one plain line gives it somewhere to go.
cells.sheetLine: The compass isn't gone. You've stopped giving it anything to read.
cells.verb: Weighing what's fair in the private ledger and letting it point the way
cells.place: In the pull toward what you actually want, the light you steer by

cells.tense: You're reading the room correctly and calling it the room's doing.
cells.ask: Write down one sentence that names the fairness you already hold — the line you keep — in your own hand on paper, and keep the paper where you'll find it tomorrow.
cells.core:
On an ordinary day you know when a thing is off and you act on it — you include the person left out, you keep the promise, you say the thing that balances the room. That read runs in everything you do: who you sit with, how you break a tie, which small favors you return without being asked. It's steady and it's accurate and it works.

And you frame it as just how things are done here. You go along with the arrangement and leave your part in it unspoken, as if no one was weighing. The quieter form underneath all the accounting is a plain read of what's right, without the arithmetic. Put that read down once, on paper, in your own hand, so the sense you've been living by has somewhere to sit outside your head.
cells.sheetLine: The fairness is holding here. You've been saying it's just how things work.
cells.verb: Weighing what's fair in the private ledger and letting it point the way
cells.place: In the pull toward what you actually want, the light you steer by
